daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Ministry of Home Affairs disclosed that 79 local governments require Rp 3.7 trillion to cover employee salaries, prompting the minister to outline three options including efficiency measures to resolve the budget shortfall. The minister also revealed that 2 million people were affected by Sumatra floods, with recovery expected to take over a year.

  • The MPR set its annual session for 14 August 2026 and will invite former presidents and vice presidents to attend.
  • DPD leadership met Vice President Jusuf Kalla to deliver an invitation to the council's annual session.
  • PKS stated that the president's directive on fuel must be followed by regulatory reform on subsidized fuel distribution.
  • A DPR member questioned government readiness to handle forest fires in the Mount Bromo area.
  • The KPK alleges that money in an envelope given to Environment Minister Raja Juli by the Kuantan Singingi regent was not fully returned, and that a ministry official received 12,500 Singapore dollars from the same regent.
  • The South Jakarta District Court scheduled a pretrial hearing for Febrie Adriansyah on 18-19 August, after his legal team challenged his suspect status.
  • The KPK seized 8,500 Singapore dollars from the office of the South Jakarta immigration office chief and confiscated 150,000 US dollars in raids in Bandung and Tangerang related to the Banjarmasin tax office case, while a witness returned Rp 9.5 billion during questioning.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's defence minister announced that the country will deploy a domestically produced "kamikaze drone", in a move to bolster indigenous defence capabilities. The minister separately stated that he sees stronger military readiness in the Indonesian armed forces.

  • Indonesia is heading to a BRICS trade meeting to push for greater market access for Indonesian products.
  • Indonesia showcased its community vaccine model to international delegations as part of health diplomacy efforts.
  • The Pakistani ambassador said that Indonesia has an important role in pushing for a resolution to the Kashmir issue.
  • Indonesia brought ASEAN youth together through a cultural scholarship programme promoting regional integration.

Other

Indonesia's economy grew 5.29 percent despite global uncertainty, according to official data. The government announced it will maintain fuel subsidies as global oil prices remain elevated, while also extending food aid and holiday travel discounts for late 2026.

  • The Ministry of Finance is taking over 60 percent of Whoosh shares, with the transaction targeted for completion by September 2026.
  • Central Papua's economy contracted 15.44 percent due to a sharp drop in Freeport sales.
  • Danantara will drive AI adoption across state-owned enterprises as part of digital transformation efforts.
  • The BGN head revealed that hasty cooking caused poisoning of a family and students who ate the government's free nutritious meal (MBG) in Jayapura.
  • Several Chinese factories will relocate to Madura, signaling investment diversification in the region.
